bull.b: LOQTORZI is showing improving commercial traction, with sequential sales growth, higher new-patient starts, and better treatment duration. Sustained adoption could provide a recurring oncology revenue base and increase operating leverage as the product scales over the next several quarters.

Repeated reductions in R&D and SG&A indicate a leaner operating structure rather than a single-period cost action. Continued expense discipline can extend the company’s funding runway, reduce the revenue needed to support operations, and improve eventual profitability if commercial growth persists.

The divestiture has materially simplified Coherus’s legacy obligations and reduced debt exposure, while remaining liabilities are expected to be substantially settled by year-end. A cleaner capital structure can let management focus resources on oncology development and commercialization rather than legacy assets.

bear.b: Large ongoing losses and deeply negative operating and free cash flow show that the business is not currently self-funding. Continued burn may require external financing or further cost reductions, limiting strategic flexibility and increasing execution pressure over the next several quarters.

The sharp historical revenue decline and modest current scale indicate an unstable earnings base, even though recent revenue has improved. This volatility makes it harder to absorb fixed development costs, plan capital allocation, and demonstrate durable operating leverage from the commercial portfolio.

Important future value depends on clinical datasets that remain early, incompletely observed, and subject to data cleaning and maturation. If preliminary efficacy or biomarker trends weaken, development timelines, regulatory prospects, and the expected contribution of the oncology pipeline could be adversely affected.
